appstore.title: App Store Connect
appstore.intro: Apps, downloads / redownloads / updates / deletions per day and territory, crashes per day, customer reviews and the store-wide rating.
appstore.need: An Apple Developer Program membership and an App Store Connect user with the Admin or App Manager role (only they can create API keys and request analytics reports).
steps: Open App Store Connect → Users and Access → Integrations → App Store Connect API (https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/access/integrations/api).
If you see “Request Access”, request it once for the team — the Account Holder must accept.
Under Team Keys click Generate API Key (the “+” button). Name it “oxilytics”. Access: App Manager (Admin also works; Sales and Reports / Developer are NOT enough for Analytics Reports).
Download the key file AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 — you can do this only once. Store it safely.
Note the Key ID (10 characters, shown in the row) and the Issuer ID (UUID at the top of the page).
Copy the .p8 file into the secrets/ folder next to docker-compose.yml and set the variables below in .env.
Restart the container (docker compose up -d), then press Test connection on this page.
checks: Key file exists and is a valid EC P-256 private key.
Analytics reports permission: GET /v1/analyticsReportRequests returns 200 (403 → role too low).
Reviews readable for the first app.
errors: Key ID / Issuer ID mismatch, or the key was revoked.
Key role is not App Manager / Admin — generate a new key.
The key belongs to another team.
notes: Historical analytics (full sync) is produced by Apple asynchronously; the first full run can take several hours while Apple prepares the ONE_TIME_SNAPSHOT report. That is normal.
Apple keeps daily analytics for a limited time; run the first full sync soon after setup.

googleplay.title: Google Play
googleplay.intro: Installs / uninstalls / upgrades per day and country, active devices, crashes and ANRs per day, the rating, and reviews (full history via reports, last 7 days live).
googleplay.need: A Google Play Console owner or an admin who can manage users, and any Google Cloud project.
steps: Create a service account: open https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/serviceaccounts (pick or create a project, e.g. “oxilytics”) → Create service account, name “oxilytics”, no project roles needed.
Open the service account → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. Save the file as gplay-sa.json and note its e-mail (oxilytics@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com).
Enable the Google Play Android Developer API in the same project: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/androidpublisher.googleapis.com → Enable.

In Play Console → Users and permissions → Invite new users: e-mail = the service-account e-mail. Account permissions: “View app information and download bulk reports (read-only)” and “View app quality information (read-only)”. Send the invite — a service account accepts automatically.

Find the reports bucket: Play Console → Download reports → Statistics (any app) → Copy Cloud Storage URI. It looks like gs://pubsite_prod_rev_0123…/stats/installs/. The bucket name is the pubsite_prod_rev_… part.
Copy gplay-sa.json into the secrets/ folder next to docker-compose.yml and set the variables below in .env.
Restart the container (docker compose up -d), then press Test connection on this page.
checks: JSON key parses, has client_email and private_key, and an access token is obtained.
Bucket is listable and contains at least one stats/installs object.
Android Publisher reviews.list on the first package returns 200 (403 → permission missing or API not enabled).
errors: Service account not invited, or invited without “download bulk reports”; propagation can take up to 24 h.
New account — Google generates reports the next day.
403 androidpublisher API has not been used in project
JSON key was deleted/rotated in Cloud Console.
notes: Google generates report files once a day (early morning UTC); a delta run before that sees yesterday's data.
Reports exist from the day the account first had installs; the full sync walks every monthly file.
